name: El Pilar
_about: THE CATHEDRAL-BASILICA OF OUR LADY OF THE PILLAR, Zaragoza (1681-1872; towers 1907-61), from OpenStreetMap (the 131 x 69 m rectangle on the Ebro, the eleven domes' lanterns) and the published plans: the brick HALL CHURCH of three naves of one height, seven bays on two rows of cruciform piers -- pendentives under the domes, sail vaults ('bóvedas de plato') over the other bays --, side chapels and end chapels; ELEVEN DOMES in glazed tiles, each with its lantern: the great one on its tall drum between buttresses with paired columns over the retablo mayor, two middling ones over the Santa Capilla and the coro, eight small ones over the side naves; hipped and lean-to tile roofs, clerestory windows; two storeys of windows in stone surrounds, the plaza front's giant Corinthian order and its three portals (two pedimented porticoes, the great niche with Serrano's relief), the balustrade with saints; FOUR CORNER TOWERS of ~89 m -- shaft, clock stage, arched stage, belfry, balustrade and urns, the copper helm of two lanterns --, the north-west one (San Francisco de Borja) climbed by its stair and a lift to its glazed mirador. Inside: the Santa Capilla (oval of twelve columns, oval dome open in an oculus, the Virgin's pillar and image, the altar of the Venida), Forment's alabaster retablo mayor, the coro (stalls in tiers, organ, Celma's grille), the coreto (stalls, organ, Goya's fresco), pews, chapel altars (tools/archgen/el_pilar.py).

piers._about: the twelve piers of the hall, 4 x 3.7 m, up to the arches' tops (their arms below the imposts make them cruciform)

pier arms._about: the piers' arms toward the naves: pilasters 30 cm proud, up to the impost

pier imposts._about: the gilt impost mouldings, under the lowest springing (12.45)

nave arches._about: the arches across the middle nave from pier to pier, 4 m deep (the vaults' oblong ends are lost in them)

aisle arches._about: the arches across the side naves, from the piers to the arcade walls of the chapels

arcade arches 1._about: the arches along the naves, from pier to pier (and to the end walls), all crowned at 21 m: the hall's three naves are of one height

great pendentives._about: the pendentives under the great dome, and the deck round its drum's foot

middle pendentives._about: the pendentives under the two middling domes (the Santa Capilla's bay, the coro's)

small pendentives._about: the pendentives under the eight small domes over the side naves

aisle vaults 1._about: the SAIL VAULTS ('bóvedas de plato') of the bays without a dome: the whole sphere over the bay, stretched to its oblong (the formerets' crowns at 21 m, the vault's at 24-25)

aisle vault space 1._about: the sail vaults' spaces over the hall's: what is under them is inside

south wall._about: the plaza front (Teodoro Ríos' of the 1940s): two storeys of windows in stone surrounds through a giant Corinthian order, the three portals

north wall._about: the river front over the Ebro: brick, two storeys of windows, the north door in the middle

east wall._about: the east front between the towers: the door of the Romanesque tympanum's portal, windows into the end chapels

west wall._about: the west front between the towers

south arcade wall._about: the walls between the side naves and their chapels: an arch into each chapel, over the chapels' roofs a clerestory window in every bay

east arcade wall._about: the walls across the ends of the naves: a door into the end vestibule, an arch into each end chapel, clerestory windows over

chapel walls._about: the buttress walls between the side chapels, on the pier lines

chapel vaults 1._about: the side chapels' barrel vaults, crowned at 13.5 m

end vestibule vaults._about: the vestibules behind the end doors

hall._about: THE HALL: the three naves up to the decks (the vaults over it are their own spaces)

south chapels._about: the side chapels' space, up to their vaults

dome rings._about: the cornice ring round the pendentives' crown under each dome

small dome rings._about: ...under the small domes, whose drums stand in from the pendentives' circle

small domes._about: EIGHT SMALL DOMES over the side naves (bays 1, 3, 5, 7): a low octagonal drum, the dome in glazed tiles, the brick lantern under a lead cap

middle domes._about: TWO MIDDLING DOMES on the axis -- over the Santa Capilla (east) and the coro (west): a window in each face of the drum, the tiled dome, the lantern

great drum base._about: the great dome's base storey over the roofs, from the pendentives' deck

great drum well._about: the hall's space on up through the base storey to the drum's own

great dome._about: THE GREAT DOME over the retablo mayor: the tall drum of eight windows between buttresses with paired Corinthian columns, the ribbed tiled dome, the lantern (OSM: 51 - 67 m)

bay roofs 1._about: hipped roofs of glazed tile over the sail-vaulted bays, between the domes

south chapel roof._about: the lean-to roofs over the side chapels, from the outer walls' tops up to the arcade walls

wall heads._about: the coping of the outer walls under the balustrade

portico west._about: the end portals on the plaza: a Corinthian column either side of the door, the entablature and a pediment

frontispiece._about: the middle portal: the frontispiece standing forward of the front, the great round-arched niche through it, the door at its back

relief._about: Pablo Serrano's relief of the Virgin's coming, in the niche over the door

portal columns west._about: paired giant Corinthian columns either side of the niche

statue pedestals._about: pedestals on the balustrade for the saints over the plaza front

towers shaft._about: the brick shaft from the ground, its faces toward the church blind but for a door (the climbed one has two, and its street door); the string course at the body's cornice

towers clock stage._about: the clock stage over the roofs, a small window over each dial

towers arch stage._about: the stage of one great arch a face, open

towers belfry._about: the belfry, two arches a face, open

towers deck._about: the deck over the belfry: its balustrade and urns round the helm's foot

towers floors._about: the floors of the arched stage and the belfry

nw tower shaft._about: the brick shaft from the ground, its faces toward the church blind but for a door (the climbed one has two, and its street door); the string course at the body's cornice

nw tower clock stage._about: the clock stage over the roofs, a small window over each dial

nw tower arch stage._about: the stage of one great arch a face, open

nw tower belfry._about: the belfry, two arches a face -- glazed: the MIRADOR, the viewpoint visitors reach by the lift

nw tower deck._about: the deck over the belfry: its balustrade and urns round the helm's foot

clocks._about: the clock dials on every face of the towers' clock stages

helms._about: the towers' helms: the green copper bell, the open lantern, a second bell and lantern, the spike, the gilt ball and the cross

urns._about: the urns on the corners of the towers' balustrades

nw tower stair._about: the stair up the Torre de San Francisco de Borja: its turret in the outer corner, the spiral from the street door's floor to the mirador's

lift shaft._about: the lift's shaft in the tower's inner corner (the real one rises 62 m)

lift._about: the lift: from the shaft's foot to the mirador's floor (index.html: a stair shortcut)

retablo predella._about: THE RETABLO MAYOR (Damián Forment, 1512-18, alabaster): the predella of seven scenes

retablo._about: ...its body: three great niches, the Assumption in the middle, the Nativity and the Presentation

retablo posts._about: the slim buttresses framing its niches, carved with tracery, rising to the crest

santa capilla pedestals._about: THE SANTA CAPILLA round the Virgin's pillar: the pedestals of its twelve columns on an oval, open between them on every side

santa capilla entablature._about: the oval entablature over the columns

santa capilla dome._about: the oval dome, painted (González Velázquez), open in an oculus to the middling dome over it

venida._about: the altar of the Venida at the back of the chapel (Carlos Salas' marble group of the Virgin's coming)

pillar base._about: the silver-clad foot of the pillar

pillar._about: THE PILLAR: the jasper column the Virgin stood on

pillar canopy._about: the gilt canopy over her image

coro walls._about: THE CORO: its walls between the piers (alabaster reliefs outside), open toward the high altar

trascoro._about: the trascoro wall at its west end, a blind niche for its altar

coro dais._about: the stalls' raised back tier along each side

coro stalls north._about: the oak stalls (Flemish, 16th century) in tiers along the coro's walls

organ loft._about: the organ's loft on the coro's north wall

coro organ._about: the coro's organ (its case of 1529) over the stalls

coro grille._about: Juan Tomás Celma's grille across the coro's open end, its gate open

coreto stalls north._about: THE CORETO at the east end: its stalls

coreto organ loft._about: the coreto's organ loft over the east door

seating._about: pews in the middle nave, between the coro and the high altar, and before the Santa Capilla

chapel altars._about: an altar in each side chapel against the outer wall (the plaza side's portal bays are vestibules)

balustrade plinths._about: the balustrades' plinths, every run on the building (neoclassical.Balusters: the preferred L2 balustrade)
